pr_title: Improve S.DS.P tests, fix async API, and improve error messages
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/46021
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/46005

Separated cleanly into commits.

1. Add the error message carried on the DirectoryResponse to the message in the DirectoryOperationException. See note below.
2. Tell server we want v3 protocol version before attempting to Bind. (We only support v3 anyway.) Without this change, the tests give 'protocol error' against slapd.
3. Fix the async API - the refactoring in #38161 removed an unused field, but had the side-effect of removing the place we start up the thread that services the async results list. Note there is already test coverage: this test now passes - we hadn't run these tests because they require server setup.
4. Improve test configuration system and replace rotted test instructions. It is now easy to test against two different OpenLDAP based servers using docker, as well as against an Active Directory DC. (I haven't investigated testing against an AD container - I set up a DC manually). This change also clarifies that the 'domain' in the configuration file refers to the root DN, which is not the same as the user domain for the AD user account.
5. Noted whether LDAP_OPT_SERVER_ERROR gives useful text, it does not, against any of the servers on either OS. As noted in #46021, there is a bug here because  this is a Windows-only LDAP option, and the other servers map the same value to LDAP_OPT_MATCHED_DN which is unrelated. I didn't fix that here; the fix would be to somehow determine the nature of the server. This text is not included in any exception messages, and I left it that way.
6. Fix the negative error codes noted in #46021. On servers based on openLDAP headers, some of the error codes are unexpectedly negative values, leading to numerous bug reports containing the exception message `The LDAP server returned an unknown error.`. Fortunately, Windows does not use negative codes; if the code is negative, pull it into the correct range. Now the error messages are meaningful.
7. Add a bunch of unit tests for various error cases to protect this fix and also validate other error codes. I used these to generate the messages below.
8. Where the error code is still unknown, which hopefully will no longer occur, include the error code in the exception message to help us diagnose it.
9. Note the ambiguity in LDAP_OPT mentioned above.

Ran all tests on Windows and all tests on Linux, each against each of the three servers, and all now pass. 

Note that one test is conditionalized on `IsActiveDirectoryServer`. This test will skip except on Windows->AD. It skips on Linux->AD because it uses the DirectoryEntry type to look for LDAP_CAP_ACTIVE_DIRECTORY_OID and DirectoryEntry does not exist on Linux (it's part of System.DirectoryServices.dll). I did not investigate whether there is another way to do this check that would work on Linux.

After this we should have a good foundation to investigate some of the other open issues in this area.

Note about (1) above. Including the error message from the response can make the exceptions more informative, at the expense of being ugly against some servers. Below are some examples, pulled from testing against each of the three servers. The first sentence (italicised) is what you get today. The rest comes from the appended response error text. Active Directory's text is particularly ugly. However I have found some of these and others helpful when figuring out why a request is failing. If users don't show these messages to their users, the extra text might be fine. If they do, I could make it debug-only, but they would have to swap our our dll in order to get better messages. Other options are an environment variable, and simply putting it on a second line. I think I am leaning towards opting in with an environment variable - if that sounds reasonable I'll push that change.

#### Active Directory

*The distinguished name contains invalid syntax.* 0000208F: NameErr: DSID-0310022E, problem 2006 (BAD_NAME), data 8350, best match of:
        '==invaliddn=='

*The server does not support the control.* The control is critical. 00000057: LdapErr: DSID-0C090B26, comment: Error processing control, data 0, v4563

*The object does not exist.* 0000208D: NameErr: DSID-03100288, problem 2001 (NO_OBJECT), data 0, best match of:
        'DC=danmose-ldap,DC=com'

*The attribute exists or the value has been assigned.* 00002083: AtrErr: DSID-031519F7, 1:
        0: 00002083: DSID-031519F7, problem 1006 (ATT_OR_VALUE_EXISTS), data 0, Att d (description):len 34

*The attribute exists or the value has been assigned.* 00002083: AtrErr: DSID-031519F7, 2:
        0: 00002083: DSID-031519F7, problem 1006 (ATT_OR_VALUE_EXISTS), data 0, Att d (description):len 26
        1: 00002083: DSID-031519F7, problem 1006 (ATT_OR_VALUE_EXISTS), data 0, Att 10 (postalAddress):len 60

*An operation error occurred*. 000004DC: LdapErr: DSID-0C091080, comment: In order to perform this operation a successful bind must be completed on the connection., data 0, v4563

#### OpenDJ

*The distinguished name contains invalid syntax.* The provided value "==invaliddn==" could not be parsed as a valid distinguished name because character '=' at position 0 is not allowed in an attribute name
*The server does not support the control.* The control is critical. The search request cannot be processed because it contains a critical control with OID ==invalid-control== that is not supported by the Directory Server for this type of operation
*The object does not exist.* Entry cn=protocolUser7.1,ou=ProtocolsGroup7.1,DC=example,DC=com does not exist in the Directory Server
*The attribute exists or the value has been assigned.* Entry ou=ProtocolsGroup3,DC=example,DC=com cannot be modified because it would have resulted in one or more duplicate values for attribute description: Protocols Group 3

#### SlapD

*The distinguished name contains invalid syntax.* invalid DN
*The server does not support the control.* The control is critical. critical extension is not recognized
*The object does not exist.*
*The attribute exists or the value has been assigned.* modify/add: postalAddress: value \#0 already exists
pr_comments: I want to get the S.DS.AM and S.DS tests working against these servers too.

I'll check again to confirm, but IIRC S.DS.AM is Active Directory specific, and S.DS could work with some non-AD ldap servers but not all. Last time I checked, S.DS.P was the library that worked with most ldap servers since it really just is a thin layer of c# on top of two different native libraries which simply implement the ldap protocol.
Still working on getting a setup for S.DS and S.DS.AM tests to pass against AD...

@danmoseley given that this PR was only targeting S.DS.P, I think there is value in merging this and then subsequently make the required modifications for the other two libraries. Would you consider reopening and merging this as-is and then figure out the other two libraries? Maybe I'm just missing something but I don't feel this PR to be "incomplete"

In my previous attempts, I was running the tests from a machine joined to corp domain. Instead I set up a 2nd VM as the test machine, added the test DC as a DNS server, joined the test machine to the test domain, and logged in as the user on the test domain. After doing this, I have all the S.DS.P and S.DS.AM tests passing against AD. There are a few failures left in S.DS tests:

1. TestInvalidSearchFilter (which passes a bad password) and TestInvalidUserAndPassword expect a DirectoryServicesCOMException but are getting a COMException. this is because AdGetLastError is returning no error after the failed bind. I do not know why. The same failure occurs when I run the tests on .NET Framework, so it's a configuration or test issue.
2. TestMissingUserAndPasswordInfo expects to get an exception when enumerating the directory, but it does not.  As far as I can tell it is not a matter of the AD server enabling anonymous access. Again, same on .NET Framework.
3. TestComInterfaces fails because it expects the security descriptor of a new OU it creates to correspond to the user it's bound as but instead it's BUILTIN. This does not occur on .NET Framework. I do not know why.

That's from Windows against AD. All the tests of all libraries pass against the non AD servers, from Windows and Linux. I will try Linux against AD.
I think this should be ready to merge now though.

Unless I hear otherwise, I plan to leave the "extended" exception strings shown above enabled. They're ugly, but we have evidence how tricky it can be to diagnose why some of these exceptions appear, and they will sometimes help. We can see whether we get preview feedback.

So everything is tested again except S.DS.P on Linux to AD. This was working before, but something changed as I now get `In order to perform this operation a successful bind must be completed on the connection`. I verified a bind did occur successfully.

I don't think I changed anything, so I'm at a loss right now.
Next step may be trying the same thing with ldap4net on Linux.

@joperezr I am out of ideas for how to get the tests working from Linux to AD. I still get `In order to perform this operation a successful bind must be completed on the connection`. This is what I have tried

* Running tests in WSL2 on a new test VM not domain joined, rather than WSL2 on my dev box, same result
* debugged through our code to ensure the bind is happening ( VS Code debugging against WSL2 is awesome)
* wrote a minimal test that just does bind, search, same result
* ip address instead of server name, same result
 * various tracing settings on the AD server didn't show anything helpful.
* ldapsearch _does_ work. built ldapsearch and enabled packet tracing - nothing stands out except it uses `ldap_sasl_bind( ld, binddn, LDAP_SASL_SIMPLE...` for the bind wheras we use `ldap_simple_bind_s` - which seemed potentially interesting, but, ldap4net has a mode that does the former, and it still fails.
* different user instead of admin. no difference
* double check user/password - they are good, if I change either, it will fail with bad credentials
* port 3268 - this is the general catalog port - it works! but this is a read only port.
* looked at the tests for AD itself, there are some that expect this error, but nothing seeming relevant. 
* look at the AD code and it simply emits it exactly when it says - when searching without successful bind

It is definitely not an issue with my changes -
* test program using ldap4net has the same problem - it doesn't use any of our S.DS.* code.
* master branch has the same problem (ie without my changes)
* with my branch 100% pass against both slapd and opendj servers (they only fail against AD from Linux)
* with my branch 100% pass against slapd, opendj, and all against AD ([except 4 of S.DS](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/47703#issuecomment-778678410)\*) when run on Windows
(* for these 4, I've found [this](https://forums.asp.net/t/2002312.aspx?ADAM+AD+LDS+DirectoryEntry+Bind+and+ADsGetLastError+on+Windows+2003) where someone was getting the same behavior in a real deployment, which accounts for 2 of them, and one other is because we're requesting Kerberos without supplying a password, which is working as expected against AD, so I think it may be this test cannot work against AD.)

At this point I'm out of ideas short of attaching a kernel debugger to the AD server, which really is out of my depth.

Given it is definitely not something I've introduced, and coverage on all the other combinations works including AD from Windows, I believe we should commit this as is. It's clearly important that we test AD from Linux before we ship, but it seems like I can't solve that right now unless @tquerec sees something obvious that I'm missing.

What do you think?

Thanks both. At some point before we ship please let's remember to be sure to run these tests again and get Linux-to-AD passing.🙂

I wonder whether we should maintain and check in a list of all manual testing activities. Eg @eiriktsarpalis  has some manual console tests, and there are others that are easy to forget about.
It occurs to me that one avenue of investigation could be to change our API calls to match ldapsearch, which works, and then bisect. I'm done with this for now though.
@danmoseley should we have a sign off release sheet to list all things should be done before every release?
Sure, might be a good idea, but even just manual tests was all I was thinking of. Perhaps someone is interested on looking into that a bit more.

issue_context.title: LdapException messages on Unix do not include detail
issue_context.body:
Right now, many LdapException messages on Unix look like:
```
System.DirectoryServices.Protocols.LdapException: The LDAP server returned an unknown error.
    at System.DirectoryServices.Protocols.LdapConnection.BeginSendRequest(DirectoryRequest request, TimeSpan requestTimeout, PartialResultProcessing partialMode, AsyncCallback callback, Object state)
```

There is no way to tell from this message what the error was. For example in the case above say the ErrorCode was -7, then the exception message should include text like `The search filter is invalid.` .  As it is you need to run under the debugger to get it, then look up in ldap.h to translate it. Examples of bugs where the specific message would have helped: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/43621 https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/41617 https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/36947

Generally these codes are dictated by an RFC that all platforms follow. A subset are represented in our code, across two enums:

* ResultCode matches `LDAP_SUCCESS` through `LDAP_OTHER` in `LDAP_RETCODE` in Winldap.h (excepting `LDAP_IS_LEAF` and `LDAP_INVALID_CREDENTIALS`)
* LdapError matches `LDAP_IS_LEAF`, `LDAP_INVALID_CREDENTIALS`, and `LDAP_SERVER_DOWN` through `LDAP_REFERRAL_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` plus `LDAP_OPT_REFERRAL_CALLBACK` in `LDAP_RETCODE` in Winldap.h

I went through every one and they all match in name and value between Winldap.h and the Unix ones in ldap.h, except most of ResultCode have different values: `LDAP_SERVER_DOWN` through `LDAP_REFERRAL_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` have the values -1 through -17, whereas in Windows they have values 0x51-0x61

(There are various other codes on both sides that aren't represented in the enumerations, but presumably we'll spot those if they ever happen and extend the enum/add messages.)

The fix is simply to extract the `LdapError` enum into LdapError.Windows.cs and LdapError.Linux.cs with the appropriate values for the platform. We should append the error code in the case that there is no mapping (ie `The LDAP server returned an unknown error '{0}'.`)

<details>
  <summary>mappings required</summary>

For reference, here's the Unix values
```
#define LDAP_SERVER_DOWN				(-1)
#define LDAP_LOCAL_ERROR				(-2)
#define LDAP_ENCODING_ERROR				(-3)
#define LDAP_DECODING_ERROR				(-4)
#define LDAP_TIMEOUT					(-5)
#define LDAP_AUTH_UNKNOWN				(-6)
#define LDAP_FILTER_ERROR				(-7)
#define LDAP_USER_CANCELLED				(-8)
#define LDAP_PARAM_ERROR				(-9)
#define LDAP_NO_MEMORY					(-10)
#define LDAP_CONNECT_ERROR				(-11)
#define LDAP_NOT_SUPPORTED				(-12)
#define LDAP_CONTROL_NOT_FOUND			(-13)
#define LDAP_NO_RESULTS_RETURNED		(-14)
#define LDAP_MORE_RESULTS_TO_RETURN		(-15)	/* Obsolete */
#define LDAP_CLIENT_LOOP				(-16)
#define LDAP_REFERRAL_LIMIT_EXCEEDED	(-17)
```
and here's the Windows values
```
    LDAP_OTHER                      =   0x50,
    LDAP_SERVER_DOWN                =   0x51,
    LDAP_LOCAL_ERROR                =   0x52,
    LDAP_ENCODING_ERROR             =   0x53,
    LDAP_DECODING_ERROR             =   0x54,
    LDAP_TIMEOUT                    =   0x55,
    LDAP_AUTH_UNKNOWN               =   0x56,
    LDAP_FILTER_ERROR               =   0x57,
    LDAP_USER_CANCELLED             =   0x58,
    LDAP_PARAM_ERROR                =   0x59,
    LDAP_NO_MEMORY                  =   0x5a,
    LDAP_CONNECT_ERROR              =   0x5b,
    LDAP_NOT_SUPPORTED              =   0x5c,
    LDAP_NO_RESULTS_RETURNED        =   0x5e,
    LDAP_CONTROL_NOT_FOUND          =   0x5d,
    LDAP_MORE_RESULTS_TO_RETURN     =   0x5f,

    LDAP_CLIENT_LOOP                =   0x60,
    LDAP_REFERRAL_LIMIT_EXCEEDED    =   0x61
```
</details>
comments: Totally agree that our error messages in Linux could and should be much better. Thanks @danmosemsft for the detailed investigation. Without going into too much detail, the issue here is that all search requests in Linux always are handled in two steps by the native library: 1) you send the request to libldap which gives you back an id to later query for the result, and 2) you query the library using that id to see the results and if there was an error with the request, that second operation returns -1 which is were we get the error message from. That said, every time that happens we also call libldap again to get the reason of the failure (which not only gives you the error code from your table above, but actually gives you the error message itself to) we are just not returning this error code and message back to the end user which is what we have to fix. I'll add a pointer here to the line that has the required info to bubble up in case someone wants to try to fix this before I get to it.

This is the important line 

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/8d6e098d647bd59a79165c3ad6b31957999479bb/src/libraries/System.DirectoryServices.Protocols/src/System/DirectoryServices/Protocols/ldap/LdapConnection.cs#L1463

servererror and responseMessage there have the info we need.

@joperezr hmm, just based on code inspection, I'm not sure I see what work there is beyond fixing the mapping. 

1. After the line you pointed to, `serverError` seems properly treated, eg turned into an exception here if necessary
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/1923bba394c31bc2d4f62a948eac8dbe64339ab2/src/libraries/System.DirectoryServices.Protocols/src/System/DirectoryServices/Protocols/ldap/LdapConnection.cs#L1641
or looks like in #43621 it may be in the original BeginSendRequest here
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/1923bba394c31bc2d4f62a948eac8dbe64339ab2/src/libraries/System.DirectoryServices.Protocols/src/System/DirectoryServices/Protocols/ldap/LdapConnection.cs#L409
or in the case of #41617 in
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/1923bba394c31bc2d4f62a948eac8dbe64339ab2/src/libraries/System.DirectoryServices.Protocols/src/System/DirectoryServices/Protocols/ldap/LdapException.cs#L133
ending up in something like
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/1923bba394c31bc2d4f62a948eac8dbe64339ab2/src/libraries/System.DirectoryServices.Protocols/src/System/DirectoryServices/Protocols/ldap/LdapException.cs#L142-L145
so I'm fairly confident everything is wired up correctly, it's just that the mapping in LdapError is Windows specific and needs to include the Linux codes which for some reason are different.

2. There is one other potential issue though, sometimes the `ServerErrorMessage` is put in the exception too eg
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/1923bba394c31bc2d4f62a948eac8dbe64339ab2/src/libraries/System.DirectoryServices.Protocols/src/System/DirectoryServices/Protocols/ldap/LdapConnection.cs#L1159-L1168
which gets it via
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/1923bba394c31bc2d4f62a948eac8dbe64339ab2/src/libraries/System.DirectoryServices.Protocols/src/System/DirectoryServices/Protocols/ldap/LdapSessionOptions.cs#L527
and there may be a problem there as we use the Windows defines as follows
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/1923bba394c31bc2d4f62a948eac8dbe64339ab2/src/libraries/Common/src/Interop/Interop.Ldap.cs#L73-L76
whereas the Linux headers have
```c
#define LDAP_OPT_RESULT_CODE			0x0031
#define LDAP_OPT_ERROR_NUMBER			LDAP_OPT_RESULT_CODE
#define LDAP_OPT_DIAGNOSTIC_MESSAGE		0x0032
#define LDAP_OPT_ERROR_STRING			LDAP_OPT_DIAGNOSTIC_MESSAGE
#define LDAP_OPT_MATCHED_DN			0x0033
/* 0x0034 - 0x3fff not defined */
```
so when we request LDAP_OPT_SERVER_ERROR = 0x33 on Unix, it looks like we're actually getting LDAP_OPT_MATCHED_DN ("Sets/gets a string containing the matched DN associated to the LDAP handle") which is probably wrong. On Unix, it looks like we should be requesting LDAP_OPT_DIAGNOSTIC_MESSAGE = 0x32.
If so then I'm guessing 90% of fixing this is just setting up the environment...

I checked all the other `LDAP_OPT_` in the code against the ldap.h and all the others are either present with the same code or we have marked `//NotSupportedinLinux`. It is just LDAP_OPT_SERVER_ERROR which isn't on Linux but isn't marked as such.

I did find this ancient mention of the discrepancy
https://microsoft.public.adsi.general.narkive.com/Dm3hdaOD/adam-extended-server-error-and-winldap
which suggests that (at least in this case) LDAP_OPT_SERVER_ERROR is the most useful on Windows, not LDAP_OPT_ERROR_STRING/LDAP_OPT_DIAGNOSTIC_MESSAGE. So I think Windows is right, but Unix needs to use the latter.

On Windows we're also not trying LDAP_OPT_SERVER_EXT_ERROR. No idea whether that is useful or not - no plans to try.

@joperezr @tarekgh the tests for S.DS.P contain instructions for using the OpenDJ server, but I wonder whether that is legacy from the original port to .NET Core, since the tests currently seem to assume an Active Directory LDAP server because they append the domain to the LDAP URL. 

It also looks like only 9 of 526 tests hit a server, which will skip unless one is set up, do you know when we last ran those?

It took a while (since I am not familiar with LDAP) but with some test fixes all but one of the tests pass against an [OpenDJ docker container](https://hub.docker.com/r/openidentityplatform/opendj/). Going forward we should probably test both, and maybe the slapd/Open LDAP server if there is an image for it. 

Anyway once I get those all passing, I can look at this and maybe some of the other bugs that may be specific to non-AD LDAP servers.

It is correct that we only have 9 tests that actually hit a server, all the rest are just unit tests that test the interop with the native library, as well as the c# layer we have.

Those 9 tests should theoretically work against any Ldap server (even though they have only ran against Active Directory), and in order to run them, you only need to manually edit the LDAP.Configuration.xml file on the unit tests project. We opted to not run them by default since that would require for us to checkin credentials on that xml file (with the way that things are setup currently), and given the fact that this code is not usually touched, we instead have manually ran them locally every time we do make some change on the code to make sure it works. When we do it, we run against an Active Directory server that we have setup, I can share details with you for connecting with it offline.

As to when was the last time we ran them, I ran them every time I made a change when writing the Linux implementation (~6 months ago) and the code hasn't been touched since, so I would imagine they should be passing just fine today. We should definitely figure out a better way of running these regularly without having to checkin credentials as part of our outer-loop tests, one idea I had but haven't had the chance to implement yet was to set up tests against an actual Ldap server using a docker farm of clients/servers so that we don't have a network dependency and everything is just running inside different docker containers that emulate a network. This is the way that our enterprise Http tests are setup, so we should look into doing something similar for DirectoryServices.

Sounds good. If we have a way to run a docker container somehow then automated testing is easy and I would imagine as you say that might be useful for networking tests too. Running manually is ok for a while more but it probably sounds be AD + another. I found your AD instructions and I'll try those.

Here are the enterprise setup instructions if you are interested in checking out how the docker farm works, if you follow those steps you should be able to run the tests and we know they are passing since we currently have a build pipeline that runs them. That is what I want to do with DirectoryServices in the future.

With respect to the discussion about `LDAP_OPT_SERVER_ERROR` (which is actually `LDAP_OPT_MATCHED_DN` for OpenLDAP) and `LDAP_OPT_ERROR_STRING` above, I wrote various tests to trigger error conditions and ran them on both a Windows client and on a Linux client against OpenDJ, SlapD, and AD servers. 

The results - zero output from the former, and almost zero from the latter (only occasionally a string "FilterError"). So the fact that we're calling the wrong thing in some cases - not really an issue.

The place where the good messages are is on directoryResponse.ErrorMessage and that may be worth including in the exception messages.

review_comments: Not that you need to fix it here, but LdapSessionOptions currently has a split implementation between Linux and Windows, so if the server error is retrieved with different options, we can move the implementation of this internal string to the RID-specific files and use the right option on each case.

> Environment.FailFast("LDAP test c [](start = 15, length = 34)

Why we fail fast the tests when there is no provided configuration file. Sorry if I missed in earlier comments but will try to read the whole thread.

The config file is copied by the build: it should always be present. I had an error earlier where it wasn't, and the tests don't fail, just skip, which is less obvious. I can revert that if you want but I figured it was helpful
I am fine with what you have. Let's see how it'll goes.

I wonder if we should default to version 3 when creating the LdapConnection object since that will be what you want more than 90% of the time. I saw other libraries do default to 3 as well, for example: [https://github.com/flamencist/ldap4net/blob/41a6397d6ad2c3cbaad65aa39b637dfc81ffac49/LdapForNet/ILdapConnection.cs#L13](https://github.com/flamencist/ldap4net/blob/41a6397d6ad2c3cbaad65aa39b637dfc81ffac49/LdapForNet/ILdapConnection.cs#L13)
